item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00326","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C05","C01"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 is a concrete, material drafting template for the child. It is the same type of letter, addresses substantially the same maritime employers and represented employees, and follows the same sequence: prior creation of a Board of Inquiry under section 206, receipt of its report, a national-health-and-safety finding, and a direction under section 208 to seek an injunction. Most of the child’s operative language reproduces C13 nearly verbatim, with principally dates, geographic coverage, and the union’s designation changed. C05 is also closely related in subject and machinery but concerns threatened rather than continuing strikes and has less exact operative wording. C01 strongly parallels the letter structure and statutory machinery but concerns the copper industry.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"On November 22, 1956, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in labor disputes between employers ... who are (1) steamship companies ... (2) contracting stevedores, (3) contracting marine carpenters, or (4) other employers engaged in related or associated pier activities","parent_excerpt":"On October 1, 1953, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in labor disputes between employers ... who are (1) steamship companies ... (2) contracting stevedores, (3) contracting marine carpenters, or (4) other employers engaged in related or associated pier activities","explanation":"The opening provision has the same statutory predicate, action, detailed enumeration of maritime employers, and sentence structure."},{"child_excerpt":"Today I received the Board's written report in the matter. A copy of that report is attached hereto.","parent_excerpt":"On October 5, 1953, I received the Board's written report in the matter. A copy of that report is attached hereto.","explanation":"The report-receipt paragraph is reproduced with only the timing formulation changed."},{"child_excerpt":"In my opinion these unresolved labor disputes have resulted in a strike affecting an entire industry or a substantial part thereof engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and with foreign nations which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","parent_excerpt":"In my opinion these unresolved labor disputes have resulted in a strike affecting an entire industry or a substantial part thereof engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and with foreign nations, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","explanation":"The substantive emergency finding is virtually verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike where such action is necessary to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and the foreign nations, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","parent_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike where such action is necessary to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and the foreign nations, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","explanation":"The operative injunction direction is essentially identical, demonstrating both literal reuse and the same administrative/legal machinery."}]}
